key_insight: The paper introduces an OWL 2 DL ontology that standardizes how machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are described, linked to training data, and benchmarked.
engineering_relevance: It improves reproducibility, comparison, and downstream reuse of MLIP models by making methods, hyperparameters, and DFT-provenance metadata machine-readable.
method: Built three ontology modules: Method, Training Data, and Benchmark.
Linked MLIP concepts with existing standards in materials science and machine learning (MDO, CMSO/ASMO, ML-Schema, Croissant).
Added 27 axioms, including property chains connecting trained models to their methods and datasets.
evidence_signal: The ontology was demonstrated with a Moment Tensor Potentials example and evaluated using competency-question queries on a 20-paper seeded knowledge graph, OWL reasoning, and ontology comparisons.
watch_item: Practical adoption may depend on community agreement on vocabularies and the effort required to curate complete, consistent metadata from legacy papers.
paper_title: An Ontology for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
